If you can’t afford or justify the cost of Sunday ticket, NFL+ is a great option (currently 20% off)
stories.summary:
I had NFL Sunday ticket for years, and really enjoyed it. Once DIRECTV was bought out and deals became more sparse, I switched to NFL+ and love it.



	 



	The only caveat is that you can’t watch the majority of games live, which isn’t a big deal for us because we’re used to not watching the games live (and staying off our phones until after we do watch it 🤣).



	 



	There’s a deal going on right now where you can get a year’s subscription for 20% off at $79.99, which is way more affordable than NFL Sunday ticket.



	 



	The other cool thing about NFL+ is that if you don’t have all the subscriptions to watch games outside of Sunday afternoons (prime, peacock, etc.), NFL+ will still have the game available after the game is over. This has always been a huge disadvantage of NFL Sunday ticket, especially with all of the games that are streamed now.



	 



	Here’s the link. Enjoy and go Bills!
	 



	https://www.nfl.com/plus/learn-more

stories.summary:
I live outside Hartford, Connecticut. New England. 



	 



	I went to a funeral today. 75 year-old guy, well liked, nice family. Big sports fan, not a Bills fan. I didn't know him well.



	 



	He wanted his funeral to be upbeat and casual, He asked that people wear clothing supporting their favorite team. 



	 



	Maybe 150 people attended.



	 



	There were about 10 Bills jerseys. Maybe 10 UConn. 4-6 Patriots. Maybe 2 Yankees. 



	 



	Small sample size and all, but it was fun to see. The guy liked country music, or we would have broken into the Shout! song.

DJ Moore is going to be an "Elite WR" this season
stories.summary:
Writing is on the wall.



	 



	Now that we've gone through OTAs, minicamp and the St. John portion of TC, it's pretty clear the chemistry between Allen and Moore is reminiscent of Allen and Diggs when Diggs came in 2020.



	 



	No, I don't see Moore leading the NFL in receptions & receiving yards. Buffalo has better secondary weapons than we did in 2020 and Allen’s growth as a QB who sees the field so well is going to spread the ball around more than in 2020.



	 



	But I also think we're going to pass a good bit more than the last couple years and with Moore we no longer have to fall back on Mesh in those 3rd down gotta have it moments. 



	 



	Moore can still clearly get open. From all the reports it sounds like his worst rep of camp was against Benford who got an INT because Moore slipped on the wet grass in the rain. Sounds like it was a physical rep, but Moore slipped.



	 



	And I think we'll continue to revisit the whole "DJ Moore is washed!!!" narrative, but I spent a bored Friday evening (my life is so exciting) watching highlights of every single year of his career.



	 



	I just don't see a washed or diminished player. Honestly, his skillset excites me more than what we had with Diggs. Moore is a true all over the field threat. Diggs was, too, but Moore's at his best downfield. That wasn't Diggs.



	 



	Plus there's the speed and YAC ability.



	 



	I just think it all fits with Allen and this offense and we're going to hear a lot of backtracking nationally this coming season about DJ Moore the player and the cost to acquire him.

stories.title: Joe Brady's football intelligence
stories.summary:
There was some discussion in the training camp thread for today about Joe Brady's press conference, and about how he seems to be doing a little better in presenting his thoughts orally.  Earlier in the year, people reacted to his machine-gun style of talking. I did, too. It makes him sound like he isn't smart. Whenever I think that, I remember having heard someone tell a story about Brady and his football brilliance. 



	 



	Today I asked Gemini to tell me that story.  Maybe everyone has heard it. If so, I apologize. Here it is:



	
		Quote
	

	
		
			 
		

		
			That story centers on a pivotal moment early in Joe Brady’s career while he was a young graduate assistant at Penn State under offensive coordinator Joe Moorhead.
		

		
			 
		

		
			When & Where It Happened
		

		
			 
		

		
			In early 2017, Moorhead took his Penn State offensive staff to New Orleans for a professional development visit with Sean Payton and the New Orleans Saints coaching staff. The trip took place at the Saints’ facility in Metairie, Louisiana.
		

		
			 
		

		
			The Key People Involved
		

		
			 
		

		
			Joe Brady: Then a 27-year-old graduate assistant at Penn State, working largely behind the scenes on film breakdown and opponent analysis.
		

		
			Joe Moorhead: Penn State’s offensive coordinator, who brought his staff to exchange ideas with the Saints.
		

		
			Sean Payton: Saints Head Coach, known for running one of the most sophisticated offensive systems in the NFL.
		

		
			Pete Carmichael Jr.: Saints Offensive Coordinator.
		

		
			 
		

		
			What Happened in the Meeting
		

		
			 
		

		
			Moorhead had introduced a highly successful RPO (run-pass option) and hurry-up spread scheme at Penn State. Payton invited the staff down to study those college concepts, expecting a high-level exchange with Moorhead.
		

		
			 
		

		
			During the chalk talk, the Saints coaches began asking granular, technical questions about specific defensive reads, coverage adjustments, and how the offense handled niche blitz packages. Moorhead handed the whiteboard marker over to Brady, who knew the precise micro-details of the system inside and out.
		

		
			 
		

		
			Brady took over the presentation, walking the Saints staff through the exact mechanics, film clips, and logic of the system. He detailed how defenders' body language dictated options and explained technical wrinkles that Payton’s staff had not seen mapped out with that level of precision.
		

		
			 
		

		
			The Impressions Formed
		

		
			 
		

		
			The Saints staff were stunned by Brady’s mastery, composure, and technical intelligence for someone of his age and role.
		

		
			 
		

		
			Immediate Respect: Sean Payton and Pete Carmichael were so blown away by the "kid graduate assistant" that Payton immediately kept Brady on his radar.
		

		
			 
		

		
			The Job Offer: Shortly after that meeting, Payton hired Brady as an offensive assistant for the Saints in 2017. Brady spent two years in New Orleans absorbing Payton's offensive principles—an experience that directly launched him to LSU in 2019 (where he won the Broderick Award and a national championship) and eventually back to the NFL.
		

		
			 
		

		
			The Narrative: Moorhead later joked in interviews that he went to New Orleans to give a presentation and ended up losing his best assistant because Brady blew everyone in the room away.
		

		
			 
		
	



	 



	 



	The way I heard the story, maybe it was Carmichael who told it, was that while Brady was running the meeting, people on the Saints staff who weren't in the meeting heard some kid was knocking it out of the park, so they joined the meeting. It was by all accounts a stunning performance



	 



	The guy knows football.

stories.title: Transportation options to Highmark on gameday???
stories.summary:
Travelling from Australia to Buffalo and will be going to the week 3 game against the Chargers.  What’s the best way to get to and from the stadium in game day?  Was planning to Uber it early in the Sunday to get to the stadium at around 10.30am, then roll the dice with ride-share on the back, noting it will probably take multiple hours and cost me my fist born… Am staying in lower west side in Buffalo - any other options I should consider?  Have got a couple of prices from private car providers however the price for the car for a day day is horrendous.



	 



	Update : thanks for all the advice - will get there earlier to make sure I don’t miss anything. Chat GPT tells me from where I live to Highmark is near on travelling half way around the earth (16,300km or 10,130 miles) so waking up an hour earlier seems worth it….

stories.title: How much would you pay Alec Pierce?
stories.summary:
Alec Pierce will be the focal point of our discussion until free agency.  We need a boundary WR with speed and he specializes in it.  He’s a lot of what we need.  I’ve read speculation that he’ll cost 20-22M aav, but I think he’ll cost in excess of 24M aav.  Can we even make a move like that happen with our cap sitch?   
	 



	Looking at the WRs that might be available via FA, trade and the draft, Pierce seems like the best option overall.



	 



	JJ or Pickens would be ideal, but I just don’t think either are in the cards for our team.  Would we trade way up for Tyson, Tate or Lemon?  Will Boston fall to us and if he does, is he an instant impact player?  Can Concepcion play outside?  Are any of the 2nd rd guys capable of making a huge difference next season?



	 



	Other free agents-



	rashid shaheed



	Deebo (I don’t like him as a fit)



	dyami brown



	tutu atwell



	christian kirk



	hollywood brown 



	Jauan Jennings



	Wandale Robinson (can he play outside)



	Ridley



	 



	Other potential trade targets-



	Pittman (if they would prefer pierce)



	jordan addison



	aiyuk



	dj Moore.



	 



	ideally, we would add 2 names listed in the post.  If we could only be so lucky.  🍀
